metadata.novelty_explanation:
NOVEL

The proposal replaces feature-based occupancy rates with a learned directional motion model, using probabilistic assignments to infer movement from anonymous enemy observations. It also preserves and propagates enemy beliefs outside visibility and accounts for blocked moves and door opening.

Planning changes include distance-decayed risk penalties, a new diagonal-door restriction, and a visit-dependent waiting threshold. These materially change prediction, memory, computation, and action selection; whether they improve performance requires empirical testing.

patch_attempts.patch_description: Separates mapping, censored anonymous motion learning, occupancy filtering, forecasting, and control. The learner estimates attempted directions while retaining blocked-attempt probability at the origin. Hidden occupancy persists outside the declared sensor radius. A short-horizon planner combines immediate contact avoidance, future occupancy forecasts, and global navigation. Fast and slow evidence stores limit stale-law influence. Performance improvements require evaluation.

Replace pooled occupancy rates with an adaptive attempted-direction model and a propagated anonymous occupancy belief. The learner marginalizes over compatible anonymous transitions, preserves blocked-attempt probability as staying, and treats observations outside the enemy sensor radius as missing. Discounted evidence allows adaptation after switches.

Forecasts combine visible enemies with uncertain unseen occupancy. Planning uses these forecasts, discounts their relevance along distant route segments, and considers waiting at a smaller immediate risk difference. These changes target avoidable collisions; improved performance remains to be measured.
